rationale: Jesus's answer ends "the good news is preached to the poor" (11:5, BSB); Isaiah 61:1 has "the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor" (BSB). In Greek the match is a shared verb root and noun: Matthew's ptochoi euangelizontai against the Septuagint's euangelisasthai ptochois. The Septuagint of 61:1 also has typhlois anablepsin, "recovery of sight to the blind," which the Hebrew-based BSB of Isaiah 61:1 lacks ("freedom to the prisoners"), and Matthew's first clause uses the same root (typhloi anablepousin). The Pulpit Commentary observes that "the words are taken from the LXX." Luke 4:17-21 shows the same verse quoted with a formula ("He found the place where it was written," 4:17; "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing," 4:21, BSB), and Luke 4:18 carries the Septuagint's "recovery of sight to the blind." Graded allusion because Matthew 11:5 has no formula and does not quote a full clause; strong because the wording matches the Septuagint at two points and Meyer, Barnes, Bengel and the Cambridge Bible all name Isaiah 61:1.
